ideas.key_change: Replace the plain nearest-cell rule for a bounded set of boundary items by a capacity-frozen transport inside each level-1 group, where a move's cost is its Poincare distance increase minus lambda times its successor-PPMI advantage, and lambda = eps_rec/sigma_A is derived, not tuned.

The pass takes no validation or test interaction, reads no Stage-3 statistic, and its output is frozen before Stage 3 starts; the frozen Stage-3 protocol (150 epochs, seed 42, beam 20) sees only t'. The frozen Stage-2 checkpoint and codebooks are read-only inputs, so no test signal can re-enter the SID construction.
ideas.motivation: All three negative rounds lost recall by moving the objects the quantizer owns: round one bent the residual chain, round two displaced 99.1% of items off the text geometry, round three added a fourth argmin-pinned level. Recall tracked distance-from-text-geometry, not prefix capacity. So the remaining degree of freedom that has NOT been tested is cell MEMBERSHIP: the SID vocabulary, the codebooks and every prefix count can be held bit-identical while the assignment of a small set of boundary items to those existing cells is re-decided. This proposal takes shape (A) explicitly: it acts at quantization time, after the frozen Stage-2 RQ-VAE, as a capacity-frozen optimal transport inside each level-1 group in which a curved distance sets the toll of a relabel and the training-only successor PPMI decides whether the toll is worth paying.
ideas.novelty: No earlier proposal here prices a relabel with a hyperbolic distance. Existing mechanisms move embeddings (geodesic shift to successor barycentres), move codebooks (Poincare-Frechet successor updates), change radial coordinates (context-entropy radial assignment), add cones, add levels, or set per-level curvature from transition scores. TOLLCAP-SID changes none of those: alpha, the codebooks, the cell set, the cell sizes and the token vocabulary are frozen and asserted equal to the baseline; the only things that can change are which existing cell a noise-floor item is named by. Curvature is load-bearing in exactly the one way the round's own measurements say is real - the radius/compactness term - because the Poincare chord factor 1/(1-||m_s||^2) makes entering a fine, boundary cell cost more than entering a central cell, so the curved metric acts as a price on the transport rather than as a displacement. It therefore cannot repeat prefix merging (counts frozen exactly), moving the input off the text geometry (codebooks and embeddings untouched, per-item toll bounded by the quantizer's own RMS error), or a fourth argmin level (no new level, no new token, identical SID vocabulary).

specification.text:
(1) Freeze everything: text embeddings x_i, level codebooks C1..C3, baseline triple t(i)=(a,b,d), cell set S, and per-cell sizes n_s. All of these are read-only.
(2) alpha = 1/max_i ||x_i||; phi(x) = tanh(alpha||x||) * x/||x|| (unit Poincare ball, curvature -1 fixed, scale derived from the data, no curvature knob).
(3) d_P(p,q) = arcosh(1 + 2||p-q||^2/((1-||p||^2)(1-||q||^2))), evaluated in float64.
(4) Cell centroid m_s = phi(c1_a + c2_b + c3_d) for s=(a,b,d), fixed for the whole pass.
(5) eps_rec = sqrt(mean_i d_P(phi(x_i), m_t(i))^2), the quantizer's own noise floor.
(6) Training-only behaviour: A(i,s) = log((p(s|i)+eps_p)/(pi(s)+eps_p)) from directed consecutive training transitions, p(s|i)=sum_{j in s} p(j|i), pi(s)=sum_{j in s} q_j with q the global incoming share, eps_p = 1/(total transitions).
(7) lambda = eps_rec / sigma_A, sigma_A = std of {A(i,s): s in the same L1 group, s != t(i)}.
(8) Cost and admissibility, per item i and candidate cell s in the SAME level-1 group:
    toll(i,s) = d_P(phi(x_i), m_s) - d_P(phi(x_i), m_t(i));
    Delta(i,s) = toll(i,s) - lambda*(A(i,s) - A(i,t(i))); Delta(i,t(i)) = 0;
    admissible iff toll(i,s) <= eps_rec; items with zero outgoing training transitions get A=0 everywhere and never move.
(9) Per level-1 group: expand each cell into n_s slots (so capacities are exactly the baseline sizes), build the square matrix M[i,slot]=Delta(i,s)+1e-9*1[s != t(i)], solve with scipy linear_sum_assignment in float64, decompose the item permutation into cycles, keep cycles in ascending order of max toll while the cumulative moved count stays <= 0.05*N, and set t'(i)=t(sigma(i)). Dropping whole cycles keeps every capacity exact.
(10) Emit t'(i) plus a record: rho, per-cycle tolls, prefix counts at levels 1/2/3 before and after, behaviour contrast before and after.

Total added wall clock under 1 minute.
ideas.coupling_equation: s(i,l,k)=zhat_k[cos(b_i,beta(l,k))]-zhat_k[d_{c0}(exp_0(h_i),exp_0(r(i,l-1)+e(l,k)))/R_l], with g_i=max_k cos(b_i,beta(1,k))-cos(b_i,beta(1,c(i,1)))>tau_null and d_i>=20; behaviour term is the first bracket, curved term the Lorentz distance in the second, and a flip requires s(i,l,k*)>s(i,l,c(i,l)).
ideas.coupling_path: One pathway: train transitions -> PPMI b_i -> subtree profile beta(l,k) -> eligibility g_i with permutation null -> the SAME score s(i,l,k) containing the Lorentz distance -> selected codeword -> repaired SID token -> Stage 3. Behaviour off zeroes every g_i so no item is eligible and tokens equal baseline. Geometry off replaces d_{c0} by Euclidean distance, changing the selected codeword while eligibility is intact. There is no separate behaviour loss and no separate hyperbolic loss: one score, one argmax, one token.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Worth keeping iff (i) mean behaviour contrast between an item and its prefix-siblings falls on the audited tail (train-only), (ii) Euclidean-versus-hyperbolic target disagreement is non-trivial so geometry is not a gauge artifact, and (iii) one frozen Stage-3 run reaches test_recall@10 > 0.065 (realistically above the untouched 0.0679). If only 1-2% repair and recall is flat within seed noise, the idea fails and is recorded negative with its number.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In quantization, at the Stage-2-to-Stage-3 SID export (curved re-quantization of an otherwise frozen Euclidean RQ-VAE); it is not a term added to the Euclidean encoder loss.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Hyperboloid (Lorentz) model of curvature -c0, c0=1/q99(||.||)^2: <x,y>_L=-x_0 y_0+x_s.y_s; exp_0(v)=((1/sqrt(c0))cosh(sqrt(c0)||v||),(1/sqrt(c0))sinh(sqrt(c0)||v||)v/||v||); d_{c0}(x,y)=(1/sqrt(c0))arcosh(-c0<x,y>_L). c0 is explicitly a gauge: scaling every tangent by 1/sqrt(c0) and using curvature 1 reproduces the ordering, so c0 is fixed only for numerical range and never tuned; all non-gauge content is the non-linearity of exp_0 and d_{c0}.
ideas.key_change: At the end of frozen Stage 2, build train-only successor-PPMI profiles, select items whose contrast with their level-1 subtree is significant under a degree-conserving permutation null, and re-quantize only those items (<=5% of 24556) with one score: z-scored behaviour affinity to the candidate subtree profile minus z-scored Lorentz distance to the candidate cumulative reconstruction, under a checked and reported prefix guard.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Transition counts, PPMI profiles, the permutation null, curvature quantile c0, scales R_l and guard thresholds all come from Stage-2 train items and train embeddings only. No validation or test item contributes a transition, embedding, percentile or threshold. The repaired table is produced before Stage 3 starts and is not revisited after any Stage-3 signal exists.
ideas.motivation: SHAPE (A). Three rounds moved the many (curved residual 0.05439; global geodesic pull of 99.1% of items 0.05165; global extra PPMI level 0.04823) and lost monotonically with distance from the plain text geometry, not with prefix count. Behaviour CONTRAST is the only diagnostic that predicts recall (+0.7104 plain, +0.7170 Euclidean control) while Gromov-delta weighting and ancestor-depth weighting hurt (+0.12, +0.075 wrongly signed). So this mechanism freezes the encoder, adds no level, pulls nothing to a barycentre, uses no Gromov delta and no ancestor depth, and repairs only the statistically demonstrable tail where text geometry and behaviour contrast disagree, with level-1 and per-level prefix drift measured and bounded.
ideas.novelty: Unlike round 1 (curved residual chain), round 2 (global popularity-adjusted successor barycentre), round 3 (extra PPMI-direction level pinned by argmin), poincare-frechet-successor-codebook (successor-weighted Frechet codebook), CURVCTRL-SID (level curvature from prefix-transition score) and BRad-RQ (behaviour-ranked radial assignment), this never re-ranks or moves the bulk. It audits at most 5% of 24556 items; the eligible set is fixed by a degree-stratified permutation null on behaviour contrast; the target codeword is chosen inside one Lorentzian score containing both behaviour affinity and curved distance; the budget is emergent from the null; the guard is measured; curvature is a gauge fixed by a data quantile, so there is nothing to tune.
ideas.observables: The exported SID table (how many items changed and at which level); B_final and guard values (level-1 total variation, per-level distinct-prefix ratio, changed level-1 token count); Euclidean-versus-hyperbolic target disagreement on the eligible set; behaviour-contrast coherence of each item with its prefix-siblings before and after (train-only); successor-predictability of exported prefixes; and the frozen Stage-3 test_recall@10.
risks: The eligible tail may be too small to move Stage 3; the null may reject almost everything; flips may land on low-degree items Stage 3 rarely sees; the level-1 guard may force B to zero; behaviour affinity may be dominated by a few large subtrees; hyperbolic and Euclidean rankings may agree almost everywhere, leaving geometry decorative. Each is measured and reported.
ideas.safeguards: (1) arcosh argument clamped >=1+1e-7 and exp-map inputs clipped to ||v||<=q99.9(||.||) so cosh stays near 3 and no point nears the ball boundary; (2) v=0 uses the series limit; (3) R_l floored at 1e-3 and z-score sigma floored at 1e-6; (4) empty subtree profiles use the global mean PPMI vector; (5) items with total behavioural degree <20 are never eligible (removes one-transition noise); (6) if fewer than 30 items pass the null the audit is a no-op, B_final=0 is reported and the baseline table is exported; (7) no objective has the ball origin as its minimum, encoder and codebooks are frozen, and at least 95% of items keep every token, so the round-one origin collapse cannot occur; (8) the guard bisection is monotone and terminates at B=0, and final guard values are reported rather than asserted.
ideas.spec_equations: c0=1/q99({||h_i||} U {||e(l,k)||})^2; exp_0(v)=(cosh(sqrt(c0)||v||)/sqrt(c0), sinh(sqrt(c0)||v||)v/(sqrt(c0)||v||)) for v!=0 and (1/sqrt(c0),0) for v=0; d_{c0}(x,y)=arcosh(clamp(-c0<x,y>_L,1+1e-7))/sqrt(c0); b_i=L2([max(0,log(N_ij*sumN/(row_i*col_j)))]) over top50(i); beta(l,k)=L2(mean_{j:prefix_l(j)=k} b_j) with global-mean fallback; g_i as above; tau=percentile_99.5({g_i^(r)}) over 20 degree-preserving permutations; R_l=max(median_i d_{c0}(exp_0(h_i),exp_0(r(i,l))),1e-3); s(i,l,k)=(A-mean_k A)/max(sd_k A,1e-6)-(D-mean_k D)/max(sd_k D,1e-6) with A=cos(b_i,beta(l,k)) and D=d_{c0}(exp_0(h_i),exp_0(r(i,l-1)+e(l,k)))/R_l; E={i:g_i>tau and d_i>=20}; sort by d_i*g_i desc; for B from B_max=floor(0.05N) down: q=h_i, for l=1..L: k*=argmax_{k used}s(i,l,k), k_l=k* if s(i,l,k*)>s(i,l,c(i,l)) else c(i,l), q=q-e(l,k_l); SID'=(k_1..k_L); accept if TV(level1)<=0.05 and every |distinct(prefix_l)|/|distinct_baseline(prefix_l)| in [0.95,1.05] and #{k_1!=c(i,1)}<=0.05N, else drop lowest d_i*g_i and repeat.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: frozen Stage-2 encoder outputs h_i (N x d), four codebooks e(l,k), baseline SID table c(i,l), Stage-2 TRAIN transition counts N_ij with row/column sums. Outputs: repaired SID' (N x 4) for the frozen Stage-3 protocol plus an audit report (B_final, guard values, disagreement rate, contrast coherence before/after, eligible count before the cap).

specification.text: N=24556, L=4, K codebook size per level; h_i frozen Stage-2 encoder output; e(l,k) level-l codebook vector; c(i,l) baseline codeword; r(i,l)=sum_{m<=l} e(m,c(i,m)). From TRAIN sequences only: successor counts N_ij, top-50 PPMI vectors b_i (L2), subtree profiles beta(l,k)=L2(mean_{j:prefix_l(j)=k} b_j). Eligibility g_i=max_{k!=c(i,1)} cos(b_i,beta(1,k))-cos(b_i,beta(1,c(i,1))); null = 20 permutations of b inside outgoing-degree deciles; tau = 99.5th percentile of pooled null g (documented 0.5% false-positive convention); eligible iff g_i>tau and total behavioural degree d_i>=20. Rank by d_i*g_i descending, B_max=floor(0.05N). Curvature gauge c0=1/q99({||h_i||} U {||e(l,k)||})^2. Map x~=exp_0^{c0}(x). Score s(i,l,k)=zhat_k[cos(b_i,beta(l,k))]-zhat_k[d_{c0}(x~(h_i),x~(r(i,l-1)+e(l,k)))/R_l], R_l = median baseline d_{c0}(x~(h_i),x~(r(i,l))) floored at 1e-3, zhat per-item z-score over k with sigma floor 1e-6. For a selected item greedy l=1..L: k*=argmax_{k used} s(i,l,k); flip only if s(i,l,k*)>s(i,l,c(i,l)); else keep baseline codeword and residual. Guard: level-1 count total variation <=0.05; distinct used prefix counts each level within +/-5% of baseline; changed level-1 tokens <=0.05N. On failure drop the lowest d_i*g_i item and recompute (<=B_max times). Export repaired SID table to the frozen Stage-3 protocol.

ideas.title: Null-calibrated hyperbolic contrast audit that repairs at most five percent of SID assignments inside a measured prefix guard

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: behaviour_enabled=False sets S_i^l={argmin} and delta_l=0, so every token is the plain Euclidean argmin and the SID equals the baseline partition.
ideas.ablation_both_on: behaviour_enabled=True and geometry='poincare' with c=1 — the configuration actually trained in this round; the other two switches exist and are wired but are not trained.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: geometry='euclidean' keeps the same shell, the same b_i, the same q_k and the same budget but ranks by ||b_i-q_k||^2 instead of d_c, isolating whether curvature rather than behaviour is doing the work.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the train split only, count consecutive pairs (a,b) within each user session; PPMI(a,b)=max(0, log( p(a,b)/(p(a)p(b)) )) with p(a,b)=#(a,b)/sum of all pairs and p(a)=#(a)/sum of marginals; keep the top-50 successors per item by PPMI, L2-normalise the row p_i, then b_i = exp_0(alpha * P p_i) with P a fixed seeded Gaussian projection to 16 dimensions and alpha = 0.5 / (max_i ||P p_i|| + 1e-12). Built once from train transitions, cached, never updated from validation or test interactions.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transitions in the train split, aggregated into a PPMI successor profile per item, used as that item's behaviour point in the Poincare ball.
ideas.cost_estimate: One extra bulk pass per epoch (24556x256 top-2 margins at all 3 levels, plus Poincare distances for about 1228 shell items per level), roughly 0.9M artanh evaluations per epoch, about 10-30 ms on one card, under 2% of the 0.145-0.16 s epoch; at 24 steps per epoch that is under 0.1 ms per step, so 3000 epochs add under 90 s wall clock. The PPMI behaviour points are built once before training.
ideas.coupling_equation: k*(i,l) = argmin_{k in S_i^l} d_c(b_i, q_k^l), with S_i^l = {k : ||z_i^l - c_k^l|| <= d_(1)(i,l) + delta_l} and delta_l = Quantile_{B=0.05}({m_i^l}).
ideas.coupling_path: train transitions -> b_i -> per-level code behaviour centroids q_k from currently assigned items -> Poincare distance d_c(b_i,q_k) -> argmin over the shell -> discrete code index -> straight-through gradient and SID token. Removing behaviour empties the shell (pure Euclidean argmin); replacing d_c by Euclidean changes which shell code wins; both change the same token.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the margin-shell items are the ones whose SID is behaviourally arbitrary, replacing their code with the curved behaviour-consistent candidate raises prefix behaviour predictability in the recorded train diagnostics and Stage3 test_recall@10 holds at or above the 0.0679 baseline and above the 0.065 gate, while level-1 agreement with the baseline assignment stays >=0.95 and prefix counts stay within a few percent of 251/1769/2201. Observed through the per-level flip count and the recorded prefix counts.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the per-level assignment step of the RQ-VAE quantizer during Stage-2 training, applied only to items inside the 5% margin shell; codebooks, encoder, decoder and the L=3 level count are untouched.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball distance at gauge-fixed negative curvature c=1, d_c(u,v)=(2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-u) xor v||), together with the exp_0 and log_0 maps; c is fixed at 1 because curvature is a gauge, so it is not a free constant and no curvature sweep exists.
ideas.key_change: After the usual Euclidean RQ-VAE assignment pass, take the per-level margin shell containing the smallest 5% of nearest-vs-second-nearest gaps, recompute level-l behaviour centroids from train transitions, and let the Poincare distance from each shell item's behaviour point to those centroids choose the code among the shell candidates instead of the Euclidean argmin.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition matrix, the PPMI rows, the projection and the behaviour points are computed only from Stage-2 train-split interactions before the SID run, and are frozen afterwards. Validation and test interactions are never read during SID construction, so no validation or test signal can influence which code an item receives.
ideas.motivation: Rounds 1-3 showed that moving the SID partition toward behaviour costs recall monotonically, and that the loss grows with distance from the plain text geometry. But a codebook's Voronoi boundary is exactly where the text embedding is genuinely ambiguous; those items carry a SID that is arbitrary with respect to behaviour. Fixing only that thin shell keeps 95% of the text-geometry partition intact while making the remaining ties behaviour-consistent, which is the cheapest place to buy prefix predictability.
ideas.novelty: Unlike behaviour-weighted Sinkhorn, curved residual chains, successor barycentre shifts and a fourth argmin level, this mechanism never moves the encoder, never updates the codebooks, never adds a level and never relocates a non-tied item. Behaviour acts only as a tie-break inside a hard 5% margin budget, and curvature acts as a bounded displacement budget through exp_0, so neither can drag the whole partition off the text geometry.
ideas.observables: Flipped assignments per level; level-1 agreement with the baseline assignment (must be >=0.95); observed prefix counts at L1/L2/L3 against 251/1769/2201; the behaviour-contrast diagnostic; Stage-3 test_recall@10.
risks: 5% may be too few flips to move recall beyond seed noise; the shell may be dominated by rare items with thin behaviour statistics, making flips noisy; the behaviour centroids may be unstable early in training (mitigated by origin fallback and the >=5-member rule); the curved ranking may coincide with the Euclidean ranking, which is a genuine possible negative that the geometry-off switch is designed to expose.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp ||b_i|| and ||q_k|| to 1-1e-6 before the Mobius addition; clamp the artanh argument to 1-1e-9; if delta_l <= 0 or the shell has fewer than 2 candidates, fall back to the Euclidean argmin; a code with fewer than 5 items keeps q_k at the origin so it cannot mirror unstable statistics; alpha rescales so all behaviour points stay inside radius 0.9; if a level loses more than 5% level-1 agreement or codebook usage drops below 200 of 256 codes, the shell is disabled for that level for the remaining training and the event is recorded; all arithmetic in float32 with log/exp maps computed through the tangent space at the origin.
ideas.spec_equations: B=0.05. For level l: d_ik=||z_i^l - c_k^l||; m_i^l = d_(2)(i) - d_(1)(i); delta_l = Quantile_B(m^l); shell S_i^l = {k: d_ik <= d_(1)(i)+delta_l}. At the start of each epoch, for every k with at least 5 assigned items, q_k^l = exp_0( mean_{i in A_k} log_0(b_i) ), else q_k^l = 0; q is detached. Choose k* = argmin_{k in S_i^l} d_c(b_i,q_k^l), ties broken by smaller Euclidean d_ik. Emit the code index with the base RQ-VAE straight-through estimator and continue with z_i^(l+1) = z_i^l - c_(k*)^l.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: level residual matrix Z^l in R^(24556 x d), codebook C^l in R^(256 x d), frozen behaviour points b_i in the unit Poincare ball (d_b=16), budget B. Outputs: integer assignment a_i^l in {0..255}, its prefix, and the straight-through quantized vector.

specification.text: See SPEC EQUATIONS. Inputs: text embeddings x_i for 24556 train items, L=3 codebooks of 256 codes each, train-only directed transition matrix. For each level, form the shell, compute q_k as a tangent-space Frechet mean, pick the code minimising d_c(b_i,q_k), keep straight-through gradients as in the base RQ-VAE. The budget B=0.05 is the round's stated guard, not a tuned value; delta_l is the B-quantile of the measured margin distribution.

ideas.title: Margin-shell curved behaviour re-assignment: at most 5% of items may be re-tokenised, and only the Poincare distance to behaviour code-centroids decides among near-tied codes.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: BEH=0 sets w_behaviour(i,k) = 0 for all i,k, so J_i(k) is pure normalised text distortion and every item keeps its Stage-2 code; the partition and the SID table are bit-identical to the baseline and the mechanism provably does nothing. Wired as a boolean that zeroes the curved similarity before the argmin.
ideas.ablation_both_on: BEH=1 and GEO=1, the coupled argmin above; this is the single arm trained and evaluated in this round.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: GEO=0 keeps the identical admissible set A_i and the identical b~_i placements but replaces d_{P,c} with ||b~_i - c~_k|| and sigma_k with the corresponding Euclidean mean, comparing the same information without curvature; the selected codes, and therefore the SIDs, generally differ from the both-on arm.
ideas.behavior_computation: from the Stage-2 training split, all sessions of the train portion; C_ij counts adjacent (i,j) orderings; each row becomes PPMI against the item's marginal transition share q_j; rows are L2-normalised and truncated to the top 20 successors; a rank-64 truncated SVD with fixed start vector gives b_i. Nodes are the 24,556 training items, so every item, including validation and test items, has a profile built from train edges only.
ideas.behavior_signal: popularity-adjusted directed item-to-item transition profiles (positive-PMI successor sets) per item, from training sessions only.
ideas.cost_estimate: zero added FLOPs inside the 72,000 Stage-2 steps (24 steps/epoch x 3000 epochs), and Stage 3 is untouched. One post-hoc pass: counting train transitions O(E) over the train interaction stream; one rank-64 truncated SVD of the 24,556 x 24,556 sparse PPMI matrix (order 0.5M non-zeros) taking minutes on one CPU node; centroids and geodesics O(N*K_l*d_b) ~ 24,556 x 2,201 x 64 ~ 3.5 GFLOP, under a second on one GPU; the snap itself O(N*32*(d_b+d)) ~ 75 MFLOP. Total added wall clock a few minutes, under 2 percent of the Stage-2 run; per-step cost at the frozen scale is exactly 0.
ideas.coupling_equation: k*(i) = argmin_{k in A_i} [ 0.5 * ||z_i - c_k||^2 / rho_l  -  0.5 * exp( - d_{P,c}( b~_i , c~_k ) / sigma_k ) ] with A_i = { k : ||z_i - c_k||^2 <= ||z_i - c_{k(i)}||^2 + rho_l }; w_behaviour(i,k) = exp(-d_{P,c}(b~_i,c~_k)/sigma_k) is the behaviour term and d_{P,c} is the curved term.
ideas.coupling_path: (train transitions) -> PPMI rows -> rank-64 SVD -> b_i -> exp_0^c -> b~_i, and (frozen Stage 2) -> z_i and {c_k} -> rho_l and A_i; the two meet in one expression, because A_i is filtered by Euclidean text distortion, the survivors are scored by geodesic behaviour distance to their curved centroids c~_k, and the winner is written into the SID coordinate. Behaviour off zeroes the curved term, making A_i irrelevant so k* = k(i) for every item. Geometry off keeps A_i and the same placements but replaces d_P by the Euclidean norm on the same ball coordinates, which changes the winner because the Poincare metric compresses radial (popularity/peakedness) differences and preserves angular (which-successor) differences.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If items that share a prefix but lead to the same popularity-adjusted successors make one SID coordinate predictable from that prefix in Stage 3, then reassigning items only among near-tied text codes raises that coordinate's behaviour contrast, lowers Stage-3 conditional entropy at that position, and lifts test_recall@10 above 0.065 without the deviation penalty. Worth keeping only if intra-code contrast of the snapped level rises AND text-distortion inflation stays within one median quantisation error AND the Stage-3 entropy at that position falls; at parity the mechanism is inert and the band occupancy is the evidence.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: at quantisation time only, inside the code-selection step of one existing level; it acts on the discrete SID coordinate produced after Stage-2 training, not on Stage-2 gradients and not on Stage 3.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball geodesic distance d_P(u,v) = (1/sqrt(c)) * arcosh(1 + 2c||u-v||^2 / ((1-c||u||^2)(1-c||v||^2))) with fixed negative curvature -c, c = (artanh(0.9)/q95(||b||))^2, plus the exponential map exp_0^c used to place behaviour vectors and code behaviour centroids in the ball.
ideas.key_change: For each item, form the admissible set of existing level-l codes whose squared text distance to the item's encoder output is within rho_l of its current best code, then pick the code minimising a two-term dimensionless objective: normalised text distortion (weight 0.5) minus hyperbolic behaviour-contrast similarity (weight 0.5). Deeper codes are kept stale (their residual chain is not recomputed), so the edit is a single-coordinate relabelling with no cascade.
ideas.leakage_boundary: edges come only from train-split sessions; validation and test interactions are never read to build C, x_i, b_i, rho_l, sigma_k, the impurity score or the level choice. Text embeddings are item metadata fixed before Stage 2. The snap is a deterministic function of (z_i, b_i, codebooks) computed after Stage 2 and before Stage 3 starts, and the frozen Stage-3 protocol, beam width and epoch budget are untouched.
ideas.motivation: Three rounds lost recall by moving item codes (curved residual, successor barycentre, PPMI fourth level), and the loss tracks deviation from the frozen text geometry rather than prefix count; meanwhile the programme's own 107-pair measurement says behaviour CONTRAST is the positive predictor of recall (+0.7104). The missing mechanism is one that raises the behaviour contrast of the SID assignment while moving nothing off the text geometry beyond the quantiser's own error scale, and that adds no level, deletes no code and creates no residual cascade.
ideas.novelty: Earlier mechanisms here changed the quantiser input (curved residual chain), shifted the input toward a popularity-adjusted successor barycentre, added an argmin-pinned fourth level, ranked items radially by context entropy, or updated codebooks with successor-weighted Frechet means. This candidate freezes the trained encoder and every codebook, runs once after Stage 2 as a deterministic 24,556-item pass, and edits exactly ONE coordinate of ONE existing level for the items inside a tie band as wide as that level's own median squared quantisation error. The curved part is a Poincare-ball geodesic comparison of popularity-adjusted transition profiles, with curvature fixed by the measured radial scale of those profiles, so radial (peakedness/popularity) differences are compressed and only behaviour DIRECTION separates codes. No new codebook, no new level, no removed code, no gradient term.
ideas.observables: moved-item count and fraction and band occupancy per level; level-1 assignment change count (must be exactly 0); level-1..l-1 prefix counts (must be exactly unchanged); depth-l and full-SID counts versus baseline (reported, not gated); mean intra-code behaviour contrast of the snapped level before and after; per-position conditional entropy of Stage-3 sequences at the snapped coordinate; test_recall@10.
risks: the tie band may be nearly empty at the chosen level, making the arm bit-identical to the baseline (recorded parity, with the occupancy as the measurement); the geodesic may prefer radially extreme codes and create singleton deep prefixes (counted and reported); the stale residual makes the reconstruction inconsistent for moved items although Stage 3 never reads it; the contrast gain may not survive seed noise; the positive contrast correlation may be cross-sectional rather than causal.
ideas.safeguards: the ball is scaled so no mapped point exceeds radius 0.9, hence 1 - c||u||^2 >= 0.19 > 0 and the geodesic denominator cannot vanish; the arcosh argument is clamped to at least 1 + 1e-8; ||b_i|| = 0 or sigma_k < 1e-6 makes S_i constant so those items and codes never move; rho_l is clamped to a positive floor; A_i is capped at 32 codes so a flat distance profile cannot move an item far; ties keep the Stage-2 code; geodesics are computed in float64 and the argmin uses float64 reductions; the SVD start vector is fixed so the pass is deterministic. Every constant is either measured on the train split (rho_l, sigma_k, kappa, l) or a documented default tied to the frozen protocol (M = 20 from beam 20, 32 nearest, rank 64, radius 0.9, equal 0.5/0.5 split), so nothing is chosen by trying alternatives.
ideas.spec_equations: C from train sessions; p_ij = C_ij / sum_j C_ij; q_j = colsum(C)_j / sum(C); PPMI_ij = max(0, ln(p_ij/q_j)); x_i = normalise(top20(PPMI_i)); V = svds(PPMI, k=64, v0=fixed) right vectors; b_i = V^T x_i; kappa = artanh(0.9)/quantile95(||b||); c = kappa^2; exp_0^c(v) = tanh(kappa||v||) v/(kappa||v||) with exp_0^c(0)=0; mu_k = mean_{i in k} b_i; c~_k = exp_0^c(mu_k); sigma_k = mean_{i in k} d_P(b~_i,c~_k); rho_l = median_i ||z_i - c_{k(i)}||^2; l = argmax_{l>=2} [1 - mean_k mean_{i in k} cos(x_i, xbar_k)]; for each i: A_i = the 32 nearest codes by ||z_i - c_k||^2 whose distortion is within rho_l of the minimum; J_i(k) = 0.5*||z_i-c_k||^2/rho_l - 0.5*exp(-d_P(b~_i,c~_k)/sigma_k); k*(i) = argmin J_i(k); set SID_i[l] = k*(i) and leave all other coordinates untouched; freeze the SID table and run the frozen Stage 3.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: inputs are the trained Stage-2 encoder outputs z_i for the 24,556 training items, the level-l codebook {c_k}, the train-split session stream, the three switches BEH, GEO and the level selector; output is a SID table in which at most one coordinate per item differs from the Stage-2 table, plus a diagnostic record (band occupancy, moved count, prefix counts, contrast, geodesics used).

specification.text: (1) From the Stage-2 TRAIN split only, count directed transitions C_ij = adjacent pairs (i then j) in training sessions; p_ij = C_ij / sum_j' C_ij'; q_j = column share of C; PPMI_ij = max(0, log(p_ij/q_j)); x_i = L2-normalised PPMI row truncated to its top M = 20 successors (20 is the frozen Stage-3 beam width, a documented default, not tuned). (2) b_i = V_64^T x_i with V_64 the top-64 right singular vectors of the PPMI matrix from a truncated SVD with a fixed start vector (deterministic, no seed sweep); items with no outgoing train transitions get b_i = 0. objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

Round four. One mechanism along the chain: user behaviour data -> behaviour graph -> tree-structure check -> behaviour item embedding -> Gromov delta -> hyperbolic curvature -> text embedding into a hyperbolic RQ-VAE -> behaviour supervision -> SID -> Stage3 -> test_recall@10. Target: a real test_recall@10 above 0.065 from one frozen four-GPU Stage2 run and one frozen Stage3 run. The baseline is the round-three mechanism tree TIGER_BEHDIR-L4.

THREE ROUNDS HAVE BEEN RUN, ALL NEGATIVE, all with the identical frozen protocol (Stage2 3000 epochs at 0.145-0.16 s per epoch, Stage3 150 epochs, seed 42, beam 20):
- round one, a curved residual chain on the frozen text geometry: L1/L2/L3 prefixes 251/1769/2201, test_recall@10 = 0.05439.
- round two, a concentration-scaled geodesic step moving every item toward its popularity-adjusted successor barycentre (99.1% of items moved): prefixes 230/1251/1298, test_recall@10 = 0.05165.
- round three, a FOURTH SID level whose direction is driven by each item's PPMI successor profile: prefixes 208/2766/6235/6302 (the deepest partition of the three), test_recall@10 = 0.04823.
The frozen baseline's own number is about 0.0679 and the gate is 0.065. Every mechanism so far has scored BELOW the untouched baseline, and the scores decrease monotonically with how far the mechanism moves the quantizer away from the plain text geometry, not with how many prefixes it creates. The capacity hypothesis (round three) is therefore REFUTED by measurement.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE PROPOSALS. A mechanism that only reshapes the SID partition is now strongly disfavoured by the evidence: three attempts, three losses, including one that increased deep-prefix capacity sevenfold. Proposals must therefore take one of two shapes and say which:
(A) a mechanism that leaves the partition essentially intact and adds the behaviour-curvature coupling where it cannot destroy the partition -- for example in the Stage-2 objective or in the codebook update inside a guard band that provably keeps the level-1 assignment and the deep-prefix counts within a few percent of the baseline's, with that guard measured and reported;
(B) a mechanism that changes the partition in a way the three failures did NOT test, and that states explicitly why the failure modes already observed (prefix merging, moving the input off the text geometry, a fourth level pinned by an argmin) do not apply to it.
In both cases the behaviour-off / geometry-off / both-on switches must exist and be wired, and the both-on arm is what is trained. Proposals that cannot explain why their mechanism should not repeat one of the three observed losses will be ranked below those that can.

CONSTRAINTS THE PROPOSALS MUST RESPECT: (a) the interaction graph is tree-like but a degree-preserving rewiring is exactly as tree-like, so 'the data is a tree' is unavailable; (b) curvature is a gauge (scaling the tangent by 1/sqrt(c) reproduces curvature 1 exactly), and on the 107 confirmed SID/recall pairs the behaviour-CONTRAST metrics are what predict recall (+0.7104 plain, +0.7170 Euclidean control, +0.6593 unweighted four-point) while Gromov-delta weighting and ancestor-depth weighting hurt by 0.12 and 0.075; the radial term is group compactness; (c) any objective whose minimum sits at the ball's origin collapses the encoder (round one measured it twice: one or two prefixes per level); (d) the behaviour signal must reach the TOKENS, and whatever it does to them must be checked against the three observed failure modes.

HARD CONSTRAINTS: one formal training run per candidate (3000 epochs, four-GPU DDP, global batch 4096), no ablation arms, no hyperparameter tuning, no seed sweeps; every constant derivable a priori. Stage3 keeps its frozen protocol. Stage2->Stage3 admission is technical validity only; test_recall@10 > 0.065 is the final judgement, and a negative result must be recorded with its numbers.

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. GOAL: decide which proposals can plausibly move Stage3 recall on one run.
READ: frozen evidence E6 (width-20 beam survival table) and E7 (teacher-forced per-position NLL), shared identically by all four bundles.
OBSERVED: baseline arm l1_br has recall@10 0.04671 with target-SID-inside-20-beams 0.0678, gold prefix alive at depth 1/2/3/4 = 1.000/1.000/1.000/0.068, and per-position NLL T1/T2/T3/T4 = 0.00/0.00/0.00/9.03. Every recorded arm that perturbs the assignment sits at or below resample 0.06363, l1_only 0.06233, l1_br_euclid 0.06207, successor_geodesic_coarse(_v2) 0.05500/0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500, successor_entropy 0.05122 - all under the 0.065 gate and under the claimed untouched 0.0679.
REASONING: the entropy of the SID problem lives at the last position (T4 NLL 9.03), while depth-1/2/3 prefix survival is already 1.000. A mechanism that only reshuffles early membership and leaves the final level's discrimination untouched cannot plausibly recover recall; one that can change a deep/final coordinate can. Also, the explicit Euclidean control (l1_br_euclid 0.06207) is at least as good as the hyperbolic successor variants, so geometry must be shown load-bearing rather than assumed.
OPEN: whether the claimed 0.0679 baseline is the same arm as l1_br (E6 actual recall 0.04671); the bundle does not reconcile them, so I treat 0.0679 as claimed-outside-bundle and 0.0636 as the best recorded arm.

STAGE: evidence read #2 - behavioural signal strength and degree support.
GOAL: test each proposal's behavioural statistic against the measured graph.
READ: E5 (successor entropy stratification), E8 (level-1 capacity ceiling), E9 (cohort-profile signal), E10 (mean outgoing degree 5.4526, 118315 edges, 115582 distinct, edge density 5.3266), E11 (same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067).
OBSERVED: behaviour signal is real but thin per item - mean outgoing degree 5.45, so most items have <=6 observed successors; the top-1 successor mass ranges 0.4375 (low entropy quintile) to 0.0543 (high). Level-1 K=256 puts canonical pairs in one cluster only 0.0822 of the time (negatives 0.0129), and the baseline SID beats a permuted null on first-prefix sharing only 0.0907 vs 0.067.
REASONING: item-level PPMI vectors (BEHTIE, SHELL, HCAUDIT) are estimated from ~5 edges per item, while cell-level aggregation (TOLLCAP sums p(j|i) over the ~11 items of a triple, and HCAUDIT/BEHTIE pool per code) gets more support. HCAUDIT's hard eligibility d_i>=20 is therefore the sharpest quantitative problem: against mean degree 5.45 (even doubled if predecessors are counted, ~11) the great majority of items cannot qualify, which compounds with its 5% budget and 99.5th-percentile gate to make an effectively empty repaired set likely. Its 20-permutation null also cannot estimate a 99.5th percentile (resolution 1/20 = 0.05).
OPEN: exact definition of d_i (in+out vs out only) is not in the bundle; both readings leave most items below 20.

STAGE: scope and specification audit of the four proposals.
GOAL: check scope-contract clause 5 (minimal self-contained specification) and clause 3 (single connected pathway) per proposal.
READ: the four proposal texts and their GEOMETRIC_NECESSITY blocks (E12/E13 in each bundle).
OBSERVED: TOLLCAP-SID gives numbered equations (1)-(10), inputs, float64/eps_p/1e-9/cycle-cap safeguards, derived alpha, eps_rec and lambda, and zero per-step cost - self-contained. BEHTIE-SNAP gives numbered steps (1)-(7) with data-derived curvature c=(artanh(0.9)/q95(||b||))^2, rho_l = median squared quantisation error, documented caps 20/64/32; equations present. HCAUDIT-SID gives Lorentz exp/distance, c0 from q99, z-scored score and a prefix guard, but leans on a 20-permutation null and a degree>=20 filter whose support the graph does not supply. SHELL-CURV-RQ's SPECIFICATION is literally "See SPEC EQUATIONS" plus three lines of prose: no distance equation, no centroid equation, no safeguard list; its q_k is called a tangent-space Frechet mean and is then used directly inside d_c(b_i,q_k) without stating an exp map, and its >=5-member rule and origin fallback appear only in RISKS. Its E13 also places the operation inside the per-level assignment step during Stage-2 training, so it perturbs codebook updates rather than acting on a frozen quantiser.
REASONING: SHELL-CURV-RQ fails or nearly fails criterion 5 on the text as submitted and carries the largest quantiser-dynamics risk; HCAUDIT is well specified but its own gates are mis-scaled to the measured graph; TOLLCAP and BEHTIE are complete and act once on a frozen quantiser.
OPEN: none - all four were read in full.

STAGE: final ranking of the four proposals.
GOAL: place all four exactly once, positions 1..4, each reason tied to the frozen evidence.
RESULT: 1 TOLLCAP-SID, 2 BEHTIE-SNAP, 3 HCAUDIT-SID, 4 SHELL-CURV-RQ.
REASONING: TOLLCAP is the only candidate that provably freezes the codebooks, the token vocabulary and every cell size while still letting behaviour change membership for a <=5% bounded set, so it cannot repeat the three documented losses (E6 shows full-assignment moves at 0.0467-0.0636, all under the gate) yet it can still change deep-cell membership, and it pools transition counts at cell level, which the 5.45 mean degree (E10) makes necessary. BEHTIE is second: complete equations, data-derived curvature and tie band, edits a single deep coordinate so it can move the level where the T4 NLL 9.03 entropy sits (E7), but its reach is one coordinate and its hyperbolic ranking may coincide with Euclidean. HCAUDIT is third despite the best use of the positive contrast signal: its degree>=20 eligibility, 5% budget and 99.5th percentile from 20 permutations cannot all be satisfied on a graph with mean outgoing degree 5.45 (E10), and its per-item argmax over all codes has no per-item distance shell, the exact freedom that ordered the earlier losses. SHELL-CURV-RQ is fourth: its specification is not self-contained ("See SPEC EQUATIONS"), it mixes a tangent mean into a ball distance, and its E13 puts the change inside Stage-2 assignment, the one place the three negative rounds showed costs recall.
OPEN: the 0.0679 vs 0.04671 baseline discrepancy in E6/E7 is unresolved in the bundle; it does not change the ordering because every candidate was scored against the same discrepancy.
